1.title: High-Performing and Elastic Compute
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: High-Performing and Elastic Compute. This module covers task statement three point two. You will choose E C two instance types and placement groups, scale with the right metrics and conditions, size Lambda and containers, run large jobs with Batch and E M R, and decouple components so each scales on its own. The exam describes a load and asks for the compute, the size and the scaling rule.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Choose E C two instance types and placement groups for a workload. Configure Auto Scaling with the right metrics and conditions. Size Lambda memory, and choose between Lambda, Fargate, E C S and E K S. Use Batch and E M R for large-scale processing. And decouple components so each one scales independently.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lantern and Loom Handles the Peaks
1.text: At Lantern and Loom, search traffic doubles every weekend. A nightly catalog job crunches numbers for hours. Image-resize requests arrive in bursts. And the data team analyzes terabytes of logs. Your job is to pick the compute, the size and the scaling rule for each.

1.title: EC2 Instance Families
1.text: E C two instances come in families, grouped by what they are optimized for. General purpose, such as M and T, balances compute, memory and network. Compute optimized, the C family, suits C P U-bound work such as batch, encoding and H P C. Memory optimized, such as R, X and U, suits large in-memory data sets and databases. Storage optimized, such as I and D, gives high local disk I O. Accelerated computing, such as P, G, Inferentia and Trainium, uses G P U, short for graphics processing unit, s and A I chips for graphics and machine learning. And the H P C family suits tightly coupled high-performance computing. T instances earn C P U credits to burst above a baseline, and a G in the name, as in M seven G, means Graviton. Exam tip: read the bottleneck, then pick the family.

1.title: Right-Sizing and Placement Groups
1.text: Right-size by matching C P U, memory, network and storage to measured use, and revisit it over time. Graviton, which is Arm-based, often gives better price-performance. Placement groups influence where instances land. A cluster placement group packs instances close together in one zone, for low-latency, high-throughput networking. A partition placement group spreads groups across separate hardware, for Hadoop, Cassandra and Kafka. A spread placement group puts a small group on distinct hardware to limit correlated failure. Placement groups are optional and free. Exam tip: lowest latency between nodes is cluster; fewest shared failures is spread or partition.

1.title: EC2 Auto Scaling Groups
1.text: An Auto Scaling group is a fleet with a minimum, a desired and a maximum size. A launch template defines what to launch. Instances are balanced across Availability Zones and registered with the load balancer automatically. Health checks replace unhealthy instances to keep the desired capacity. You can mix On-Demand and Spot instances, and instance refresh rolls out new A M I s. There is no extra charge for Auto Scaling. The figure shows a launch template feeding a group spread over two zones behind a load balancer. Exam tip: for a self-healing, elastic fleet, use an Auto Scaling group across zones behind a load balancer.

1.title: Scaling Policies
1.text: There are several ways to scale. Manual scaling means you change the desired capacity, which suits occasional, simple changes. Scheduled scaling runs actions at set dates and times, when the timing is predictable. Target tracking holds a metric at a target, like a thermostat, and suits most dynamic workloads. Step and simple scaling respond to alarm thresholds with set steps, when you want finer control. Predictive scaling forecasts from history and scales ahead, for cyclical traffic and slow start-up. Predictive plus dynamic scaling together is faster than either alone. Exam tip: to hold average C P U near a value, use target tracking; for a known daily peak, use scheduled or predictive.

1.title: Metrics and Conditions for Scaling
1.text: Which metric should drive scaling? Predefined target tracking metrics include average C P U, network in and out, and A L B request count per target. E C two metrics arrive every five minutes, so turn on detailed monitoring for one-minute data. Memory and disk need the CloudWatch agent. The metric must rise and fall with the number of instances. For queues, track a backlog per instance metric, not the raw queue length. Set an instance warmup, so new instances are not counted too early. The figure shows the queue length divided by the worker count feeding a metric that drives the group. Exam tip: choose a metric that grows when load grows and shrinks when you add instances.

1.title: Application Auto Scaling and Scaling Plans
1.text: Application Auto Scaling scales other resources with the same policy types: E C S service task counts, DynamoDB capacity, Aurora replicas, Lambda provisioned concurrency, and Spot Fleet. The older A W S Auto Scaling console feature, with scaling plans, tied several resources together. The documentation now explains how to migrate scaling plans to E C two Auto Scaling and Application Auto Scaling policies. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, check how the exam names this feature. Exam tip: scaling a resource other than E C two points to Application Auto Scaling policies.

1.title: Serverless and Container Compute
1.text: Each service has its own sizing. Lambda memory runs from one hundred twenty-eight to ten thousand two hundred forty megabytes. C P U grows with memory, at about one v C P U at one thousand seven hundred sixty-nine megabytes. There is a fifteen-minute limit, and Lambda scales by concurrency. With Fargate, you pick C P U and memory per task, with no servers to manage. Amazon E C S service auto scaling adds or removes tasks, and cluster auto scaling adds instances. Amazon E K S uses Kubernetes scaling on managed nodes, Fargate or Auto Mode. Amazon E C R is a private registry for images, with scanning and replication. Find the right Lambda memory by monitoring, Power Tuning or Compute Optimizer. Exam tip: a slow C P U-bound Lambda function often needs more memory, which brings more C P U.

2.title: AWS Batch and Amazon EMR
2.text: A W S Batch runs batch jobs at any scale. You submit jobs to a queue, and Batch provisions E C two, Spot or Fargate capacity. Choose it for thousands of independent jobs, simulations and rendering. Amazon E M R is a managed big data platform for Hadoop, Spark and related frameworks, on E C two, E K S or serverless. Choose it for large-scale data processing, analytics and E T L. Both remove cluster management and scale to the job, and Spot capacity suits fault-tolerant batch work. Exam tip: a queue of containerized jobs is Batch; Spark or Hadoop analytics is E M R.

2.title: Decoupling and Distributed Compute
2.text: Decouple with S Q S, S N S and EventBridge, so producers and consumers scale independently. Scale consumers on queue backlog, not on the producers. Put compute close to users with multiple Regions and Availability Zones. CloudFront moves content and edge logic near users; module nine covers it. Local Zones, Wavelength and Outposts bring compute close to cities, five G networks and on-premises sites; module twelve covers them. And fan out work with Lambda, a Step Functions Map state, or Batch. Exam tip: if one part must scale on its own, put a queue or topic in front of it.

2.title: Choosing Compute
2.text: Here is the chooser. Full control and special hardware means E C two. An elastic fleet of servers means E C two Auto Scaling behind a load balancer. Short, event-driven code means Lambda. Containers without servers means Fargate on E C S or E K S. Kubernetes means E K S. Queued batch jobs means A W S Batch. Spark and Hadoop means Amazon E M R. And tightly coupled H P C means the H P C family in a cluster placement group. Exam tip: match the unit of work: server, function, container, job or cluster.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: High-Performing Compute
2.text: Here is what the exam asks. Which instance family or placement group. Which scaling method and metric. Which size: an instance size, Lambda memory or a task size. Which service: E C two, Lambda, Fargate, Batch or E M R. And which decoupling service lets a tier scale alone. Exam tip: underline the bottleneck and the shape of the load before choosing.

2.title: Design Check: Lantern and Loom Handles the Peaks
2.text: Here is the Design Check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Search traffic doubles each weekend: Auto Scaling with target tracking on request count per target. A known Friday evening peak: scheduled or predictive scaling. Order workers fall behind: scale on queue backlog per instance. Image resizing in bursts: Lambda, with memory tuned for speed. A nightly job of thousands of tasks: A W S Batch with Spot capacity. Terabytes of logs to analyze: Amazon E M R. And an in-memory search index: memory optimized instances.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. For instances, pick the family by bottleneck, and use cluster, partition or spread placement. For scaling, target tracking suits most workloads, scheduled and predictive suit known patterns, and the metrics must track load. For serverless and containers, size Lambda memory, and use Fargate, E C S or E K S. For big jobs, Batch handles queued jobs and E M R handles Spark and Hadoop. And queues let each part scale alone.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Lantern and Loom runs an in-memory product search index that needs a very large amount of memory for each v C P U. Which E C two instance family fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: memory optimized. These instances provide a high amount of memory for each v C P U. Compute optimized suits C P U-bound work, and storage optimized suits local disk I O.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. The web fleet of Lantern and Loom should keep average C P U utilization near fifty percent as traffic changes, with no manual action. Which scaling approach fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: a target tracking scaling policy on average C P U utilization. It holds a metric near a target by adding and removing instances automatically.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Workers in an Auto Scaling group process messages from an Amazon S Q S queue. The team wants the worker count to follow the backlog. Which approach works best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: target tracking on a custom metric of messages per worker instance. A scaling metric must rise and fall in proportion to the number of instances, and the raw queue length does not.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Select two. Which two statements about A W S Lambda memory configuration are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. Lambda allocates C P U in proportion to memory, so raising the memory of a C P U-bound function can shorten its run time. Memory is configurable from one hundred twenty-eight to ten thousand two hundred forty megabytes, and the standard limit is fifteen minutes.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Every night Lantern and Loom must run thousands of independent containerized jobs. It wants a queue, automatic provisioning of cheap Spot capacity, and no cluster to manage. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A W S Batch. It accepts jobs into queues and provisions E C two, Spot or Fargate capacity to run them. E M R targets Spark and Hadoop.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: A. Question two: C. Question three: B. Question four: A and C. Question five: D. In Module eight, we choose high-performing databases.
